newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan urges caution on low-rated hospitals.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan urges caution on low-rated hospitals.

text.p: Although lower-rated hospitals continue to show some financial improvement, changes to Medicare and Medicaid and other trends could mean trouble ahead, J.P. Morgan Securities said in a new report.
"As a whole...most of the good news appears to be over for our lower-rated hospital sample," the firm said in its quarterly survey of non-profit hospitals.

The survey found that low-rated hospitals showed better financial results in year-over-year comparisons, "but quarterly comparisons showed only slight improvement, indicating that year-over-year improvements will become more difficult in 1997."

In addition, the number of hospitals reporting better earnings rose to 19, up from 10 in 1995, and 11 hospitals reported net income above seven percent. But seven hospitals reported net income below two percent, the most since the first quarter of 1996.
J.P. Morgan said its concern about weaker hospitals "has been growing during recent months as it seems more extensive changes in the Medicare and Medicaid programs are likely to be implemented."
